summary: This Part II supplies the proof-specific weight-four constructions behind the explicit Zagier theorem: specialized relations, cluster cells, motivic correlators, decorated flags, Grassmannian configurations, residues and a regulator comparison. Lower weights, the determinant statement and the general conjecture are imported from Polylogarithms and its K-theoretic suppliers. Explicit and inductive presentations remain distinct, and unresolved comparison and construction leaves are recorded rather than assumed.

nodes.title: Single and double symbols
nodes.statement: For n=3,4 let Rawₙ(F)=Q[F× ⊔ (F××F×)], with single generators Sₙ(x) and double generators D₂₁(x,y) or D₃₁(x,y). Temporarily adjoin zero/infinity single symbols with value zero for specialization notation. Put s(a,b,c,d)=((a−b)(c−d))/((a−d)(c−b)) using homogeneous determinants on P¹, and Z(a₁,…,a₆)=−(a₁−a₂)(a₃−a₄)(a₅−a₆)/((a₂−a₃)(a₄−a₅)(a₆−a₁)). Cyc is an unnormalized cyclic sum; Cyc⁻₆ uses alternating rotation signs. The projected cross-ratio r used in Z.4 satisfies r(a,b,c,d)=s(a,c,b,d).

nodes.title: One-parameter specialization
nodes.statement: For x=tᵃu, y=tᵇv with a,b integers and u,v regular units at t=0, put u₀=u(0), v₀=v(0). On U(F(t)), specialization sends x to u₀. On single symbols it sends Sₙ(x) to Sₙ(u₀) if a=0 and to 0 otherwise. On D₂₁ it gives D₂₁(u₀,v₀) if a=b=0; −S₃(v₀) if a>0,b=0; −S₃(u₀) if a=0,b>0; 2S₃(u₀/v₀) if a=b<0; and zero otherwise. On D₃₁ the corresponding five cases are D₃₁(u₀,v₀), S₄(v₀), −S₄(u₀), 3S₄(u₀/v₀), and zero. These are raw-symbol linear maps for the fixed parameter, not a claim of parameter independence in weight one.

Combinatorial constructions use an infinite field F. Motivic realizations and the final comparison use a number field F.
proofSteps: Decompose nonzero rational functions by order and leading unit.
Apply the displayed disjoint cases to the basis and extend linearly.

nodes.title: The Q₃ presentation
nodes.statement: L₃(F) is Raw₃(F) modulo the span of D₂₁(x,y)−D₂₁(y,x), the Q₃ relations and all their one-parameter specializations as in specialization. For six distinct P¹-points, Q₃ is Cyc₆(D₂₁(s₁₂₃₄,s₄₅₆₁)−S₃(s₁₂₄₅)+2S₃(s₁₃₄₅))−4S₃(Z₁₂₃₄₅₆). Specializations range over F-rational punctured one-parameter families and their valuation/leading-unit limits, including further specializations of the resulting relation family; this explicit relation closure is part of the presentation.

Take the native module quotient and export its quotient universal property.

nodes.title: Reduction to the explicit trilogarithm group
nodes.statement: There is a natural isomorphism from the supplier’s explicit 22-term B₃(F) to L₃(F), carrying [x]₃ to S₃(x). Under its inverse D₂₁(x,y) becomes [1−1/x]₃+[1−1/y]₃+[(1−y)/(1−x)]₃−[(1−1/y)/(1−1/x)]₃+[y/x]₃−[1]₃, with degenerate cases obtained by specialization. This is not an identification with the inductive B₃. The constant [1]₃ is retained.
hypotheses: All groups and complexes in this roadmap have rational coefficients; U(F)=F×⊗Z Q.
Combinatorial constructions use an infinite field F. Motivic realizations and the final comparison use a number field F.
proofSteps: Specialize Q₃ to the divisor D₁₃ (equivalently D₂₆ followed by y=1, Lemma 5.1) to obtain (29) in L₃; further specializations give the inversion and three-term relations (19) in L₃.

Substituting (29) into Q₃ gives the coordinate 22-term relation of P.3 (Lemma 5.2(i)). Hence [x]₃↦S₃(x) kills R₃(F) and defines B₃-exp→L₃, which is surjective because (29) expresses every double symbol by single symbols.

For the inverse send S₃(x)↦[x]₃ and D₂₁(x,y)↦ the right side of (29). The symmetry relation maps to zero by inversion and Q₃ maps to the 22-term relation. The specialization table (26) is compatible with this assignment in every order case (for a>0=b the right side specializes to [1−1/v₀]₃+[1−v₀]₃−[1]₃=−[v₀]₃ by (19), matching −S₃(v₀); for a=b<0 to 2[v₀/u₀]₃=2[u₀/v₀]₃). So every specialization of Q₃ maps to a specialization of the coordinate 22-term relation.

That these specializations lie in R₃(F) is the step GR attributes to Gon95 §5; P.3 records the degenerate cases of its coordinate relation as statements still to prove, so it is requested from P.3 (P3-SPEC). The analytic functional equations of P.3 over C are not used: they cannot prove an algebraic identity over an arbitrary infinite field.
acceptance: Both composites fix all single generators and the reduction determines all double generators.

The map descends to L₃, commutes with all relation specializations and agrees with the imported explicit δ₃ under trilogarithm-reduction. Rational U notation converts multiplication to addition.

The remaining B₂ expressions are five-term relations; handle the specialized cases by the valuation table.
Use the inverse reduction to compare with the supplier differential.

nodes.title: Oriented Stasheff cells
nodes.statement: K_m is the cellular associahedron for a labelled convex (m+3)-gon: a face is a noncrossing partial dissection and is a product of associahedra indexed by its regions. Its dimension is m minus the number of chosen diagonals. Choose an orientation on the top cell and induced boundary orientations, with the cellular incidence differential d and the Koszul product boundary. This is a finite combinatorial cellular complex, not a new topological moduli-space assumption.
hypotheses: All groups and complexes in this roadmap have rational coefficients; U(F)=F×⊗Z Q.
Combinatorial constructions use an infinite field F. Motivic realizations and the final comparison use a number field F.
proofSteps: Represent diagonals by unordered nonadjacent vertex pairs and enforce the noncrossing predicate.
Orient face products consistently and define signed incidence maps.
Opposite ways of adding two diagonals have opposite signs, proving d²=0.
acceptance: Cellular orientations must match the flip square in cluster-boundaries.

nodes.title: Triangle and triangulation two-forms
nodes.statement: For a generic ordered tuple of vectors lᵢ in a two-dimensional symplectic space put Δᵢⱼ=ω(lᵢ,lⱼ)∈F×. An oriented triangle contributes Δ₁₂∧Δ₂₃+Δ₂₃∧Δ₁₃+Δ₁₃∧Δ₁₂ in Λ²U; W_T is the sum over a triangulation T. For T with diagonal 13 and T′ with diagonal 24 of the cyclic quadrilateral (1,2,3,4), set X=Δ₁₂Δ₃₄/(Δ₂₃Δ₁₄). With the edge oriented from T′ to T, W_T−W_T′=(1+X)∧X=δ[−X]₂. Its image in Milnor K₂ is triangulation-independent. The vectors are taken in a two-dimensional symplectic space modulo Aut(V₂,ω), as in GR §1.3; the forms Δᵢⱼ are invariant under that group, not under all of GL₂.

nodes.title: Weight-four maps on cells of dimension at most two
nodes.statement: On Stasheff cells associated to generic P¹-points define L₄⁴(T)=W_T∧W_T, L₄³(e)=[−X_e]₂⊗(W_T+W_T′). The orientation is the one for which δL₄³=L₄⁴d. A pentagonal face has L₄²=Σ_{k mod 5}[s(k+1,k+2,k+3,k+4)]₃⊗s(k+3,k+4,k,k+1)/s(k−1,k,k+1,k+2). On the square face of a heptagon determined by j put L₄²=[s(j,j+1,j+2,j+3)]₂∧[s(j+3,j+4,j+5,j+6)]₂, with orientation reversal negating it. For product faces include the remaining W factors using the weight grading. These values lie in the weight-four Chevalley–Eilenberg terms: Λ⁴U, B₂⊗Λ²U, and (L₃⊗U)⊕Λ²B₂.

nodes.title: The hexagon three-cell
nodes.statement: For a hexagon define L₄¹(a₁,…,a₆)=Cyc⁻₆(D₃₁(s₁₂₃₄,s₄₅₆₁)−S₄(s₁₃₄₅)−S₄(Z₁₂₃₄₅₆)) in L₄. A one-step rotation negates this value. Product three-cells are formed by the same weight-four rule as cluster-low-cells. The four-cell value is zero, so the required top equation on the heptagon is Σ_{k mod 7}L₄¹(a_{k+1},…,a_{k+6})=0, equivalently Q₄.

nodes.title: Cluster boundary identities
nodes.statement: The maps cluster-low-cells and cluster-three-cell satisfy δL₄ʲ=L₄^{j+1}d in every cell dimension, using the raw generator formula for δ₄ before its descent. The edge, square and pentagon identities are GR Lemmas 3.12, 3.13 and 3.15; the pentagon identity uses the five-term relation (79), not Q₃. The hexagon identity is Proposition 4.4, whose proof uses Q₃ through trilogarithm-reduction, and the heptagon identity is Q₄ (Proposition 5.5). They therefore yield the weight-four cellular-to-Chevalley–Eilenberg chain map of Theorem 1.17 once δ₄ has descended.
hypotheses: All groups and complexes in this roadmap have rational coefficients; U(F)=F×⊗Z Q.
Combinatorial constructions use an infinite field F. Motivic realizations and the final comparison use a number field F.
proofSteps: For edges use the difference of squares (Lemma 3.12); for square faces use the tensor derivation rule (Lemma 3.13).
Expand a pentagon and reduce by the five-term relation (Lemma 3.14 for the invariant W_{K₂}, then Lemma 3.15).
For the hexagon compare the L₃⊗U and Λ²B₂ components separately as in Proposition 4.4, rewriting the double-symbol term with Q₃.
Use d²=0 on K₄ and the Q₄ boundary formula to prove the relation image vanishes (Proposition 5.5); do not assume δ₄ is already defined on its quotient.
acceptance: The proof has no use of the full cluster polylogarithm conjecture or motivic universality.

sources.locator: §3.4, Lemmas 3.12–3.15, pp. 42–44; §4.3, Theorem 4.3 and Proposition 4.4, pp. 52–53; §5.2, Proposition 5.5, p. 56; Theorem 1.17, p. 21

nodes.title: The weight-four Lie coalgebra
nodes.statement: Define δS₄(x)=S₃(x)⊗x and δD₃₁(x,y)=D₂₁(x,y)⊗(x/y)+S₃(x/y)⊗((1−x)/(1−y))+S₃(x)⊗(1−1/y)−S₃(y)⊗(1−1/x)+[x]₂∧[y]₂. This raw map kills Q₄ and all its specializations; together with δ₂ and weight-three-cobracket it defines a graded Lie coalgebra on U⊕B₂⊕L₃⊕L₄ through weight four. Co-Jacobi is the graded Chevalley–Eilenberg d²=0, not the assertion that the displayed map itself squares as an untyped function.
hypotheses: All groups and complexes in this roadmap have rational coefficients; U(F)=F×⊗Z Q.
Combinatorial constructions use an infinite field F. Motivic realizations and the final comparison use a number field F.
proofSteps: Use the hexagon identity and d²K₄=0 to kill generic Q₄ under the raw formula.
Check each order case in the specialization tables, including the coefficient 3 for equal poles.
Descend by the quotient universal property. Check co-Jacobi on the single and double generators using δ₃.
acceptance: Both δ₃₁ and δ₂₂ components survive; on equal poles the limit is δ(3S₄(u₀/v₀)).

sources.locator: §1.2, item 3, equations (37)–(38) and the specialization check, pp. 13–14; §5.2, Proposition 5.5, p. 56; Theorem 1.14(a), p. 16
sources.match: (38) gives the cobracket of {x,y}_{3,1}: four B₃⊗F× terms and the Λ²B₂ term {x}₂∧{y}₂. Proposition 5.5 shows it kills Q₄ through the cluster map for m=4, hence also the specializations, since δ commutes with specialization; Theorem 1.14(a) asserts the resulting graded Lie coalgebra structure.

This is the object Polylogarithms:P.4/explicit-weight-four-complex uses in degree one; that node consumes this one, so no dependence on it is introduced here. It is not defined as the kernel of δ₂₂ before exactness is proved and is not the inductive higher Bloch group.

Restrict the cobracket and use the zero Λ²B₂ component to factor it through B₃-exp⊗U.

nodes.title: The weight-four extension theorem
nodes.statement: The sequence 0→B₄-comb(F)→L₄(F)→Λ²B₂-exp(F)→0 is exact, where the last arrow is δ₂₂ and sends D₃₁(x,y) to [x]₂∧[y]₂. Thus Γ-exp(F,4) includes quasi-isomorphically in the weight-four Chevalley–Eilenberg complex: its quotient is the identity two-term complex on Λ²B₂. This supplies the proof promised by the parent’s freeness-extension node; it does not identify B₄-comb with an inductive presentation.
hypotheses: All groups and complexes in this roadmap have rational coefficients; U(F)=F×⊗Z Q.
Combinatorial constructions use an infinite field F. Motivic realizations and the final comparison use a number field F.
proofSteps: Specialize Q₄ along the collision families used in §6.
Modulo B₄-comb prove D₃₁ is alternating, invariant under the required inversion/complement identities, and satisfies the B₂ five-term relation in each argument.
Factor the map on pairs through Λ²B₂. It is inverse to δ₂₂ on the double generators, proving the kernel assertion.
Identify the quotient of Chevalley–Eilenberg by Γ-exp with an identity complex and contract it.
acceptance: Surjectivity follows from wedges of B₂ generators; exactness is proved rather than taken from the supplier.

Corollary 1.15 deduces that (44) is a quasi-isomorphism.

nodes.title: Cyclic words and special derivations
nodes.statement: Fix a finite rational puncture set S={a,s₁,…,s_n} and a tangent at a. Let V be the rational puncture-loop space generated by X_s, s∈S, with Σ_s X_s=0, using X_{s₁},…,X_{s_n} as a basis. Form C(V)=⊕_{r≥1}(V^⊗r)_{cyclic rotation}. First quotient by the pure-puncture cyclic words ⟨X_s,…,X_s⟩ for s≠a, and then by every first-shuffle sum Σ_{σ∈Sh(p,q)}⟨v₀,v_{σ(1)},…,v_{σ(p+q)}⟩ for p,q≥1. In positive correlator weights retain word length r≥2 and assign weight r−1, with the usual Tate regrading (1). Call this reduced object CLie_S. The pure-puncture reduction matters in length two (higher pure powers are already killed rationally by shuffle); it removes the central kernel of the derivation action. The cut cobracket is the sum of ⟨v_i,…,v_j⟩∧⟨v_j,…,v_{i−1}⟩ over the cyclic cuts of GR (66), keeping only positive-weight factors. It descends through cyclic and shuffle relations and satisfies co-Jacobi. Labels may repeat but equality of the cut labels is not required. The identification of its graded dual with special derivations is the separate comparison target below.
hypotheses: All groups and complexes in this roadmap have rational coefficients; U(F)=F×⊗Z Q.
Combinatorial constructions use an infinite field F. Motivic realizations and the final comparison use a number field F.
proofSteps: Use the puncture relation to identify V with a native finite free rational module, take cyclic coinvariants of its tensor powers and then quotient by the pure-puncture and specified shuffle submodules.
Define the cyclic cuts on words, omitting weight-zero factors. Check the cyclic relation, each first-shuffle generator and co-Jacobi by pairing cuts.
Keep the correlator weight r−1 distinct from tensor length r. This target is linear algebra on words; the special-derivation and motivic identifications are the separate targets below.
acceptance: The repeated-puncture cases are admitted, and the base point is not an extra puncture letter in every word.

sources.locator: §2, item 2, the cyclic envelope and its shuffle relations, p. 27; equation (66) and Figure 7, p. 28
sources.match: GR forms the cyclic tensor envelope of H₁ of the punctured line, divides by the first-shuffle relations to obtain CLie^∨, and describes the cut cobracket (66) illustrated in Figure 7.

sources.match: Proposition 8.3 shows that the kernel of the derivation map on cyclic words is spanned by pure-puncture polynomials, which is why the reduced object removes the pure length-two words (E04).

nodes.title: Cyclic words and tangential special derivations
nodes.statement: For the punctured line with distinguished tangential puncture a, the graded dual of the positive reduced cyclic shuffle coalgebra identifies canonically with the positive graded special derivations of its free fundamental Lie algebra. In puncture generators these satisfy D(X_a)=0 and D(X_s)=[X_s,u_s] for s≠a, where X_a=−Σ_{s≠a}X_s; the Lie relation is preserved. The bracket on derivations is dual to the cyclic-cut cobracket. The requirement D(X_a)=0 is essential: preserving conjugacy classes alone gives a larger space.
hypotheses: The rational punctures are distinct and the tangent at a is nonzero.

The free graded Lie algebra on the puncture generators modulo the single relation is native; its Hodge and motivic realizations enter only in motivic-correlator. Graded pieces and duals are taken degreewise.
proofSteps: Express a tangential derivation by the tuple u_s, modulo the ambiguity of adding a multiple of X_s. Pure-puncture cyclic powers are exactly the associative centralizer kernel removed before passing to the Lie/shuffle part.
Use the nondegenerate pairing of free Lie words with tensor words modulo shuffle to turn the constraint Σ_s[X_s,u_s]=0 into cyclic invariance.
Identify the commutator of two derivations with the paired cut operation, including its Tate/weight regrading.
acceptance: Every derivation in the image fixes the distinguished puncture generator, and both inverse constructions agree on cyclic word generators.
For two punctures the free Lie algebra has one generator and no positive special derivations; the reduced cyclic side is also zero.

sources.locator: §2, item 2, the special-derivation conditions and Theorem 2.1 with (62)–(63), pp. 26–27
sources.match: GR defines special derivations as those killing the tangential generator X₀ and preserving the conjugacy classes of the puncture generators, and quotes the isomorphism κ of Theorem 2.1 from G08 Proposition 8.4.

sources.locator: §8.2, Lemma 8.1 and Propositions 8.2–8.4, pp. 84–85
sources.match: Lemma 8.1 gives the derivation κF by X₀↦0 and X_s↦[X_s,∂F/∂X_s]; Proposition 8.3 identifies its kernel with the pure-puncture polynomials and proves the reduced map is an isomorphism; Proposition 8.4 states the shuffle-quotient version, which needs the same reduction in length two (E04).

nodes.title: Motivic correlators on the punctured line
nodes.statement: For a number field F, a∈P¹(F), a nonzero tangent vector v at a and b₀,…,b_m distinct from a (repetitions among bᵢ allowed for m>1; require b₀≠b₁ when m=1), define Cor^M_{a,v}(b₀,…,b_m) in the weight-m Lie coalgebra of MT(F), by dualizing its action on the motivic unipotent fundamental group and the cyclic-word/special-derivation pairing. For m>1 it is independent of v. Its cyclic-cut cobracket is GR (66). For the standard tangent at ∞ fixing the affine coordinate and b₀≠b₁, Cor∞(b₀,b₁)=b₀−b₁ in U in the source’s weight-one normalization; the weight-two value agrees with the imported dilogarithm, with the sign in GR (67). The pure-puncture word classes are zero in the reduced cyclic carrier; the ordinary weight-one numerical formula is asserted only off its diagonal.
hypotheses: All groups and complexes in this roadmap have rational coefficients; U(F)=F×⊗Z Q.
Combinatorial constructions use an infinite field F. Motivic realizations and the final comparison use a number field F.
proofSteps: Invoke MT-1 and MT-2 for the actual mixed Tate category, its Lie coalgebra and the motivic fundamental group.
Apply the dual action to cyclic words; use specialness to descend through the shuffle quotient.
Use the free fundamental group calculation to derive the cut formula and the weight-one/two normalization.
acceptance: This constructs a subcoalgebra of correlators, not a proof of the universality conjecture for all weights.

sources.locator: §2, items 2–5, equations (62)–(68) with Theorem 2.2 and Definition 2.3, pp. 26–29; §1.2, item 5, pp. 14–15
sources.match: GR recalls the motivic fundamental group of the punctured line with tangential base point and the special-derivation action (62)–(63), defines motivic correlators by dualizing it, lists cyclic invariance (65), tangent independence in weights above one, the cut cobracket (66) and the low-weight values (67), and fixes the correlators {x}_m and {x,y}_{m−1,1} in (68).

nodes.title: Hodge correlator integrals
nodes.statement: For the punctured complex line, realize the motivic correlator by the trivalent plane-tree integral: leaves are labelled by the cyclic bᵢ, internal vertices range over P¹(C), edges carry the Green function log|x−y| with the specified tangential normalization at a, and the integrand is the alternating product of one Green function and d^C of the remaining edge functions, summed with the plane-tree orientation and automorphism weights. Here d^C=∂−∂̄. The precise normalization is the Hodge realization and canonical real period convention of GR §2.3; it is checked against its weight-two value rather than inferred from an unnormalized integral.
hypotheses: All groups and complexes in this roadmap have rational coefficients; U(F)=F×⊗Z Q.
Combinatorial constructions use an infinite field F. Motivic realizations and the final comparison use a number field F.
proofSteps: Use request HODGE for the framed Hodge–Tate realization and canonical period.
Construct the finite tree sum and the locally integrable integral, with the normalization specified by the realization.
Check its cut differential and weight-two period; the collision limit is a separate theorem.
acceptance: Keep Green-function normalization, d^C and Tate powers in the API.

nodes.title: Collision continuity of Hodge correlators
nodes.statement: For m>1, Cor^H(z₀,…,z_m) is continuous on C^{m+1} minus the locus where all entries coincide. In a partial collision the specialization is the correlator on the component nearest the tangential base point, with coincident arguments retained. The theorem makes no continuity claim at the full diagonal. In particular it justifies the specialized Q₃/Q₄ relations used by the motivic realization.
hypotheses: All groups and complexes in this roadmap have rational coefficients; U(F)=F×⊗Z Q.
Combinatorial constructions use an infinite field F. Motivic realizations and the final comparison use a number field F.
proofSteps: Use the admissible degeneration and canonical extension requested in HODGE.
Control logarithmic singularities and reduce the possible limit discrepancy to a constant on a boundary stratum.
Apply the circular-average cancellation in Lemma 29 to kill that constant.
acceptance: A triple of points collapsing to the same value can have direction-dependent dilogarithmic cross-ratio limits; the excluded locus is essential.

sources.locator: §2.1.3, Theorem 11, p. 18; §4, Lemma 29 with its proof and the closing corollary, pp. 44–45
sources.match: Theorem 11 asserts that Hodge correlators are continuous off the full diagonal; Lemma 29 shows that the limit discrepancy on a boundary stratum vanishes by averaging over circles, and the corollary states that only the component nearest the base point determines the limit, with the example of L₂((a−c)/(b−c)) having no limit.

nodes.title: Change of correlator base point
nodes.statement: Let ℓ≥3, a≠b, and x₁,…,x_ℓ be rational points different from a and b, with repetitions permitted. For I⊆{1,…,ℓ}, let x^I replace x_i by a exactly when i∈I. Then Cor_a(x₁,…,x_ℓ)=Σ_I(−1)^|I|Cor_b(x^I). These correlators have weight ℓ−1. When an argument approaches its own base point, the regularized specialization Cor_a(a,x₂,…,x_ℓ) is zero provided at least one other argument differs from a. This is a specialization statement, not an unrestricted definition on the full diagonal.
hypotheses: Number field F; nonzero tangential basepoints, with tangent independence in weights ℓ−1>1.
Ordinary arguments avoid their current base point. Boundary arguments are interpreted by the stated regularized specialization, and the all-coincident locus is excluded.
proofSteps: Use the Green-function identity G_a(x,y)=G_b(x,y)−G_b(a,y)−G_b(x,a)+constant.
Integrals from internal-edge correction terms split with one zero factor; expanding the external edges yields exactly the subset sum.
Compare cobrackets and apply Hodge rigidity and injectivity of the number-field regulator on primitive extensions to obtain the motivic identity.
At an argument/base-point collision use the regularized logarithm in weight one and induction on cuts; the remaining constant is killed by a first-shuffle relation.
acceptance: For ℓ=3 the nonzero terms give the dilogarithmic five-term identity; a simultaneous full collision is excluded.

sources.locator: §2, item 7, Theorem 2.6 with (70)–(72), p. 32; Lemmas 2.7 and 2.8 with (73), p. 33
sources.match: Theorem 2.6 expresses Cor_a as the signed sum over subsets of arguments replaced by a of Cor_b, proved from the Green-function identity (71) and transported to motives by regulator injectivity and the rigidity Lemma 2.7; Lemma 2.8 shows the specialization at an argument meeting the base point vanishes when another argument differs.

nodes.title: Weight-four correlator depth reduction
nodes.statement: For ℓ>3 arguments, every weight-(ℓ−1) motivic correlator is a rational linear combination of correlators with at least two equal arguments, after a projective coordinate change and the specified base-point specialization. In weight four (ℓ=5), repeated use of this reduction and first-shuffle identities expresses every correlator as a combination of −Cor∞(0,0,x,1,y) and −Cor∞(0,0,0,1,z). The excluded ℓ=3 case is weight two, where this depth reduction is false; the argument count and the motivic weight must not be confused.
hypotheses: All groups and complexes in this roadmap have rational coefficients; U(F)=F×⊗Z Q.
Combinatorial constructions use an infinite field F. Motivic realizations and the final comparison use a number field F.
proofSteps: Use correlator-basepoint-change and its zero boundary specialization to show that, modulo repeated-argument correlators, exchanging the basepoint with one argument negates the class.
For even ℓ, cyclic invariance and the induced permutation sign kill the class. For odd ℓ>3, the first-shuffle relation pairs all but an even-multiple remainder, which vanishes rationally.
At ℓ=5 reduce the repeated words with cyclic and shuffle relations, and normalize the remaining distinct points projectively to obtain the stated two types.
acceptance: The depth bound is ℓ>3 on the number of arguments, hence weight greater than two. It is applied at ℓ=5, not extrapolated to the dilogarithm.

sources.locator: §2, item 7, Proposition 2.9 with footnote 12, pp. 33–34; Corollary 2.10, p. 34
sources.match: Proposition 2.9 shows that for more than three arguments every correlator is a combination of correlators with a repeated argument (false for three arguments, footnote 12); Corollary 2.10 concludes that every weight-four correlator is a sum of the correlators {x,y}_{3,1} and {x}₄.

nodes.title: Realization of the combinatorial Lie coalgebra
nodes.statement: For a number field F, S_m(y)↦−Cor∞(0 repeated m−1 times,1,y), D₂₁(x,y)↦Cor∞(0,x,1,y), and D₃₁(x,y)↦−Cor∞(0,0,x,1,y) define a natural morphism from the combinatorial graded Lie coalgebra through weight four to the mixed Tate motivic Lie coalgebra. Its image is exactly the correlator subcoalgebra in these weights. It is not asserted injective or surjective onto the entire motivic Lie coalgebra.

nodes.title: The weight-four Bigrassmannian complex
nodes.statement: Use exactly the supplier’s C_m(q), preserving vector scales. Set BC_m^(4)=⊕_{4≤q<m}C_m(q), in homological degree m, as the quotient of the full complex by the rows q<4. Use ∂=Σ_{i=0}^{m−1}(−1)^i deletion_i and p=Σ_i(−1)^i projection_i; ∂²=p²=0 and ∂p+p∂=0, hence D=∂+p. Outgoing components in the quotient vanish. Grassmannian duality gives the dual truncation q≤m−4 and interchanges deletion and projection.

nodes.title: Generic decorated flags
nodes.statement: A decorated p-flag in an N-dimensional F-space is 0=F₀⊂F₁⊂…⊂F_p with dim F_i=i and a specified nonzero vector f_i∈F_i/F_{i−1}. An m-tuple is generic when every sum F_{1,a₁}+…+F_{m,a_m} with 0≤aᵢ≤p and Σaᵢ≤N is direct. Let C_m(A_N^(p)) be the rational free module on generic tuples modulo simultaneous GL_N action. The underlying generic-tuple augmented complex, before coinvariants, uses the alternating deletion differential. Decorated flags are native chains of submodules and nonzero vectors in native quotients.

nodes.title: From decorated flags to configurations
nodes.statement: For N≥4 put p=N−4 and use flags of length p+1=N−3. For m flags and each a=(a₁,…,a_m) with aᵢ≥0, Σaᵢ≤p, project the decoration f_{i,aᵢ+1} to V/(⊕_i F_{i,aᵢ}), obtaining a generic m-tuple in dimension N−Σaᵢ. Sum its class over all such a. This gives t_{m−4}:C_m(A_N^(N−3))→BC_m^(4), omitting zero target rows q≥m. It is a chain map with the declared face convention and commutes with stabilization after the specified standard flag choices.

nodes.title: The generic-flag comparison on group homology
nodes.statement: Over an infinite field the augmented complex of generic decorated-flag tuples before taking GL_N coinvariants is acyclic: every finite cycle is coned off by a flag generic to its finite support. Comparison from a genuine projective Q[GL_N]-resolution therefore yields a homology map to the flag-configuration complex and, through flag-comparison and duality, to the dual weight-four Bigrassmannian complex. Do not claim that the flag tuple modules themselves are free Q[GL_N]-modules. Independence of the auxiliary comparison is by comparison homotopy.
hypotheses: All groups and complexes in this roadmap have rational coefficients; U(F)=F×⊗Z Q.
Combinatorial constructions use an infinite field F. Motivic realizations and the final comparison use a number field F.
proofSteps: Genericity is a finite collection of nonempty open conditions; infinitude supplies a common transverse flag for a finite support.
The cone contracts the finite cycle, proving exactness of the augmented complex.
Use projectivity of the bar resolution to construct a comparison into this exact complex; compare any two choices by a homotopy.
The generic group-homology comparison mechanism is request HOM, extending the supplier’s weight-three instance.
acceptance: Do not infer exactness after coinvariants from exactness before coinvariants.

Define G₄=G̃₄/(im(π₈∂:C₉(4)→G̃₄)+im(π₈p:C₉(5)→G̃₄)). Thus both the nine-term and dual nine-term relations are imposed. This is a proof-specific configuration group, not the single-symbol B₄-comb.

nodes.statement: Let Alt_m be the full signed sum over S_m and |I| the U-class of the Plücker determinant. Use the projected round cross-ratio r from P.3. R₈⁴ is projection to G₄ and all unlisted components are zero. On G₄ the boundary is the descent of R₇³p, with the face signs fixed by bc; the sign certificate is explicitly required. nodes.title: Finite symbolic Bloch modules
nodes.statement: For the finite configuration sizes needed here, b₁(q,m) is free on q-element subsets; its determinant letters are symmetric because −1 dies in U. The b₂ generators are [i₁,…,i_{q−2}|j₁,j₂,j₃,j₄]₂, symmetric in projection indices, alternating in the last four, modulo ordinary and dual five-term relations. For b₃(3,m) use the two families [i|j,k,l,h]₃ and [i,j,k,l,h,s]₃ with dihedral and seven-term relations. The first family's three-term relation holds in B₃-exp only modulo the constant [1]₃, so evaluation of b₃ lands in B₃-exp/Q[1]₃, not in B₃-exp (E01). This suffices: every use of b₃ in the chain-map identities comes after the cobracket, and δ₃[1]₃=[1]₂⊗u(1)=0, so the composite b₃⊗b₁→B₂-exp⊗Λ²U is well defined; R₇³ itself is defined by its explicit formula in actual B₃-exp⊗U, not through b₃.

Define evaluation of b₁ and b₂ into U and B₂-exp, and of b₃ into B₃-exp/Q[1]₃.
Check that the symbolic cobracket b₃→b₂⊗b₁ is compatible with evaluation followed by δ₃, which factors through B₃-exp/Q[1]₃ because δ₃[1]₃=0.

nodes.title: The configuration chain-map identities
nodes.statement: The formulas R₅¹,R₆²,R₇³,R₇²,R₈⁴ give a map of the dual weight-four Bigrassmannian complex, with total differential D=∂+p, to G₄→(B₃-exp⊗U)⊕Λ²B₂→B₂⊗Λ²U→Λ⁴U. The required identities are: δR₆²=R₅¹p on C₆(2), δR₇³=R₆²p on C₇(3), δR₇²=R₆²∂ on C₇(2), δ_{G₄}R₈⁴=R₇³p on C₈(4) (the definition of δ_{G₄}), and the conditions R₅¹∂=0 on C₆(1), R₇²∂=0 on C₈(2) and R₇³∂+R₇²p=0 on C₈(3). The last identity does not split: the Λ²B₂ part of R₇³∂ is nonzero on C₈(3) and is cancelled by R₇²p (E05). For the unscaled wedge W=Alt₇([r1234]₂∧[r1567]₂), the source's last calculation gives δW=−84 times the expression displayed on the right of its equation (244); this is why R₇²=−W/84 (E02). The constant-free symbolic b₃ suffices for these identities (E01). Consequently δ̃ descends from G̃₄ to G₄: it kills the projection relation because p²=0, and the forgetting relation because δ̃∂=R₇³p∂=−R₇³∂p=R₇²pp=0 (GR Proposition 7.8, with the corrected argument).

proofSteps: In the first square use δb₁=−3a₁+6a₃, δb₂=a₁−2a₂−a₃, δb₃=−2a₂−4a₃; hence δ(b₁/2−b₂+b₃)=−5a₁/2 (Lemma 10.10).
For the middle square expand in t₁,…,t₈ and reduce by the explicit five-term matrices of Lemma 10.12; use Lemma 10.13 with its coefficient 14.
For the diagonal square verify δW=−42 Alt₇([r2456]₂⊗|12|∧|23|), while the other expression reduces to half that alternation.

For C₈(3): the B₃⊗U part of R₇³∂ vanishes because it does not involve the seventh vector. Put X=Alt₈([r(1|2,5,6,7)]₂∧[r(2|1,3,4,5)]₂). Supply the finite symbolic certificate in Λ²b₂(3,8) (gap C8-SQUARE).
For C₈(2) and C₆(1): R₅¹∂=0 because the alternation runs over two unused vectors; R₇²∂=0 needs a finite symbolic certificate in Λ²b₂(2,8) (gap C8-SQUARE).
The three squares of GR §10 use D=∂+p with GR's alternating signs Σ(−1)^{s−1}; no further sign adapter is needed inside the dual Bigrassmannian complex.

nodes.title: The canonical weight-four period
nodes.statement: Restrict the canonical real period map from the Chevalley–Eilenberg complex of framed Hodge–Tate structures to weight four and precompose with correlator-realization. In the real-valued convention for the parent’s single-valued L_n, its single-symbol value is L₄*(z)=(5L₄(z)+(1/3)L₂(z)log²|z|)/16. In lower weights L₃*=3L₃/8 and L₂*=L₂/2. The bottom Λ⁴U component is ω₄=Alt₄(log|x₁| d^C log|x₂|∧d^C log|x₃|∧d^C log|x₄|)/6, with d^C=∂−∂̄; Tate coefficients and the Deligne grading are retained. All other components are determined by the imported canonical period DGA map, not by a guessed pointwise equality to L₄.

nodes.statement: For a finite rational single-symbol sum a=Σ_z q_z[z]₄ whose explicit boundary Σ_z q_z[z]₃⊗z is zero, and every embedding σ:F→C, one has Σ_z q_z L₂(σz)log²|σz|=0 and hence Σ_z q_z L₄*(σz)=(5/16)Σ_z q_z L₄(σz). More generally the same argument applies to any free single-symbol representative of an element of ker δ₄-exp. The equality is proved on representatives and descends; it does not assume that a tensor relation holds termwise.
hypotheses: All groups and complexes in this roadmap have rational coefficients; U(F)=F×⊗Z Q.
Combinatorial constructions use an infinite field F. Motivic realizations and the final comparison use a number field F.
proofSteps: Apply δ₃⊗id to the zero boundary to get Σ q_z[z]₂⊗z⊗z=0 in B₂⊗U⊗U.
For each embedding apply the trilinear map L₂⊗log|·|⊗log|·|, obtaining exactly the vanishing correction.
Insert this identity in the canonical single-symbol period formula and use rational linearity.
acceptance: The comparison scalar is the explicit nonzero rational 5/16; it is not imported as an unproved pointwise normalization.

nodes.title: The normal-crossing coefficient diagram
nodes.statement: For a smooth complex variety X and a fixed finite simple-normal-crossing support D, form the finite coefficient diagram on the smooth strata Y of D needed by the Chern cocycle. A codimension-q stratum carries Γ-exp(k(Y),4−q), with weight-zero Q in internal degree zero; a term of internal degree j has total degree j+2q. Use the imported low-weight symbol differentials and uniformizer-first residues θ_v(π∧u₁∧…)=ū₁∧…, θ_v(all-unit wedge)=0; single Bloch symbols specialize to the residue class for valuation zero and to zero otherwise. Require every intermediate symbol and residue in the chosen finite diagram to have the specified SNC support. With these closure hypotheses the horizontal and signed residue arrows form a complex; the extra singular-stratum homotopy H of a general regular-variety construction is zero in this case. This target constructs only the coefficient diagram used below, not a Gersten resolution or a motivic quasi-isomorphism for all regular X.
hypotheses: All groups and complexes in this roadmap have rational coefficients; U(F)=F×⊗Z Q.
Combinatorial constructions use an infinite field F. Motivic realizations and the final comparison use a number field F.
proofSteps: Use the existing explicit complexes for weights one through four.
On each incident smooth pair use the uniformizer-first residue and low-weight specialization formulas.
Check δ², each mixed square and cancellation of two successive residues in local normal-crossing coordinates; choose the total sign to make these identities hold.
Do not use the unresolved general finite-place transfers. The remaining SNC closure and sign certificate is gap RES.
acceptance: The codimension-four Q term has total degree eight, not four.

nodes.title: The weight-four current regulator
nodes.statement: On the admissible normal-crossing diagram, the canonical period forms are locally integrable and define currents. For each codimension-q stratum take (2πi)^q times its pushed-forward period current. Together with the logarithmic holomorphic dlog component β on the exterior column these define a map r_D to the weight-four real Deligne cone. For a term of total degree k its ordinary current degree is k−1; the Deligne complex uses its corresponding shifted degree k. The current identity is dP−Pδ=2πiΣ_Y i_{Y*}P res_Y with the incidence signs fixed in normal-crossing-diagram. Nonproper simplicial BGL pieces require the logarithmic Deligne extension in request DELIGNE; the parent’s projective-only comparison is insufficient.

Combinatorial constructions use an infinite field F. Motivic realizations and the final comparison use a number field F.
proofSteps: Establish local integrability of each symbol period and its products by logarithmic forms.
Use Stokes on coordinate punctured disks and extend as currents; calibrate the residue sign on a uniformizer.
Add the exterior dlog component to the real-current component to obtain the Deligne cone map.
Use DELIGNE and RES to fix the nonproper comparison and all pushforward signs before calling this a regulator comparison.
acceptance: A current on codimension q acquires degree 2q and twist (2πi)^q under pushforward.

nodes.title: Weight-three scissors configurations
nodes.statement: A₃(F) is the rational scissors group of two ordered projective tetrahedra ⟨L;M⟩ in P³(F). Impose projective invariance, antisymmetry separately in each tetrahedron, vanishing when one tetrahedron lies in a hyperplane, the alternating additivity relation obtained from five vertices in either tetrahedron, and the dual additivity relation obtained by the corresponding projected configurations. Work on the source’s admissible configurations; a degenerate term is admitted only when the defining relation supplies its specialization. Its two reduced coproduct components land in A₂⊗U and U⊗A₂, with A₂ mapped to the imported B₂ by the dilogarithmic scissors map a₂.
hypotheses: All groups and complexes in this roadmap have rational coefficients; U(F)=F×⊗Z Q.
Combinatorial constructions use an infinite field F. Motivic realizations and the final comparison use a number field F.
proofSteps: Construct the free module on admissible simplex pairs and quotient by both primal and dual relations.
Use common refinements to define the reduced coproduct; use the existing dilogarithmic scissors comparison rather than define B₂ again.
Request SCISSORS supplies the exact admissibility and A₂ normalization absent from the named stage’s coarse brief.
acceptance: Both tetrahedra have alternating orientations, and dual additivity is independently imposed.

nodes.title: The scissors-to-trilogarithm map
nodes.statement: Use Goncharov's map a₃:A₃(F)→B₃-exp(F) of G00 §3.3: a₃=(1/6)a′₃−(1/3)a″₃. Here a′₃ is the alternating double sum over omitted vertices (i,j) of r₃(l_i|L without l_i; M without m_j), where r₃=(1/15)Alt₆[T]₃ is one third of the class normalized by GR (167) (r₃=T₃/3 in Z.4's notation, GR (236)); a″₃ is the same alternating double sum of μ₃(l_i,m_j|L without l_i; M without m_j), with μ₃(x₁,x₂,x₃;y₁,y₂,y₃)=(1/2)Alt_{S₃×S₃}[r(x₁,y₂,x₂,y₁)]₃. In GR's normalization, with a′₃ built from the (167)-normalized class, the same map is (1/18)a′₃−(1/3)a″₃; the printed (1/2)a′₃−(1/3)a″₃ with footnote 24 is inconsistent with (236) and with G00's coproduct theorem (E06). All block alternations are signed sums, not averages. This map kills the scissors relations and intertwines the reduced coproduct with the explicit δ₃. Its collinear degeneration is r₃=−2μ₃ (G00 Lemma 3.7), equivalently GR Lemma 9.3.
hypotheses: All groups and complexes in this roadmap have rational coefficients; U(F)=F×⊗Z Q.
Combinatorial constructions use an infinite field F. Motivic realizations and the final comparison use a number field F.
proofSteps: Build both finite alternating sums in the actual explicit B₃ group, with r₃=T₃/3.

Prove that a′₃ and a″₃ kill the degeneration, antisymmetry and dual additivity relations (G00 Proposition 3.4 and Lemma 3.5), and that only the combination (1/6)a′₃−(1/3)a″₃ kills additivity (Proposition 3.6 with Lemma 3.7).
Prove the coproduct compatibility δ₃a₃=(a₂∧a₁)∘ν (G00 Theorem 3.2), which fixes the ratio of the two coefficients.
Apply the collinear degeneration formula with its rational coefficient to the residues below.
acceptance: The ratio of the coefficients of a′₃ and a″₃ is (1/6):(−1/3) when a′₃ is built from r₃; the μ₃ factor 1/2 is retained.

nodes.title: The Grassmannian symbol and motivic lift
nodes.statement: On the rational variety of generic eight-vector configurations in dimension four, the weight-four integrable symbol is I₄=Alt₈(|1234|⊗|2345|⊗|3456|⊗|4567|). Adjacent projections to Milnor K₂ vanish modulo constants; the symbol is projective and obeys both nine-term relations. The required refinement is an F-defined, tangentially regularized motivic iterated-integral lift whose cobracket equals the scissors expression Δ=(a₃∧id+id∧a₃+id) r_Δ of GR §9.3, hence equals δG₄. Equality of symbols alone does not determine this lift, its constant extension or its descent to G₄. This refinement is gap LIFT.
hypotheses: All groups and complexes in this roadmap have rational coefficients; U(F)=F×⊗Z Q.
Combinatorial constructions use an infinite field F. Motivic realizations and the final comparison use a number field F.
proofSteps: Prove integrability and both configuration relations by G09’s determinant/coproduct identities.
For a generic matrix move first-row entries to zero one at a time; each determinant is linear along each segment, reducing integrals to punctured P¹.

Supply tangential regularization at singular endpoints, field-of-definition control and constant terms; G09’s theorem on Hodge–Tate geometric variations by itself does not establish all these motivic assertions over F.
Compare the full cobracket with the explicit scissors expression and apply weight-four correlator depth reduction.
acceptance: Only after LIFT is proved may the symbol-level object be used as a combinatorial L₄-valued configuration map.

nodes.title: The generic polylogarithmic Chern cocycle
nodes.statement: Compose flag-comparison, duality and the configuration map with the regularized motivic lift, and use correlator depth reduction to obtain an L₄-valued weight-four cocycle on the generic simplicial flag space for GL_N, N≥4. Remove its Λ²B₂ component by an explicitly scaled double-symbol cochain h: the projected component in R₇³ has coefficient −3/28, and h uses that coefficient on the matching D₃₁ pair so δ₂₂h is exactly the unwanted wedge. Subtract its coboundary and use the extension theorem to factor the degree-one term through B₄-comb. The result has values in Γ-exp(F,4), not merely in the larger Chevalley–Eilenberg complex. GR's printed correcting element Alt₈{r(3,4|2,5,6,7),r(6,7|1,3,4,5)}₃,₁ omits this coefficient (E07).
hypotheses: All groups and complexes in this roadmap have rational coefficients; U(F)=F×⊗Z Q.
Combinatorial constructions use an infinite field F. Motivic realizations and the final comparison use a number field F.
proofSteps: First form the cocycle in the larger weight-four coalgebra complex.
Use exactness to identify the Λ²B₂ component and choose h on the actual double generators with coefficient −3/28.
Subtract the coboundary, checking signs and normalizations before claiming cancellation.
The surviving term lies in B₄-comb and the complex agrees with the supplier’s Γ-exp.
acceptance: Cancel a wedge with its actual coefficient; an unscaled double generator does not cancel −3/28 of that wedge.

nodes.title: Extending the Chern cocycle across residues
nodes.statement: The generic Chern cocycle extends over the simplicial BGL_N coefficient diagram by successive smooth SNC residues. The R₇³ residue on |123|=0 vanishes using collinear degeneration. The R₆² residue on |12|=0 is the alternating B₂⊗U expression in GR (231)–(232), pulled back from five-vector data, and its next residue is supplied by four-vector cross-ratios. In the Milnor column R₅¹, successive residual lifts X∈Λ³U, Y∈Λ²U and Z∈U on codimensions one, two and three have final divisor zero. The correction coboundary has zero residues by Lemma 9.6. Every used intermediate stratum must be shown smooth with SNC support and compatible simplicial pullbacks (RES); no general singular transfer theorem is silently used.
hypotheses: All groups and complexes in this roadmap have rational coefficients; U(F)=F×⊗Z Q.
Combinatorial constructions use an infinite field F. Motivic realizations and the final comparison use a number field F.
proofSteps: Compute the R₇³ residue by its normalized scissors/trilogarithm degeneration.
Compute R₆² residue at l₂=L l₁, then identify its pullback extension and the next residue.
Use G93’s universal flag-residue construction for X,Y,Z and its alternating simplicial boundary relation.
Check Lemma 9.6 for the scaled correcting coboundary, using the specializations of D₂₁ at zero, one and infinity.
Verify all SNC closure and signs in RES before totalizing.
acceptance: The extended cocycle has total degree eight, including the codimension-three U-term in degree seven and its degree-eight divisor condition.

sources.locator: §9.2, items 1–4, Lemmas 9.2–9.3 and Corollary 9.4, pp. 88–90; §9.3, Lemma 9.6, p. 93
sources.match: §9.2 computes the residues of the generic cocycle: the Milnor column through the residual lifts X, Y, Z of G93, the B₂⊗F× column on |12|=0 (Lemma 9.2, (232)), lifted from five-vector data, and the B₃⊗F× column on |123|=0, which vanishes by Lemma 9.3 (Corollary 9.4); item 4 extends the cocycle to BGL_n.
Theorem 4.5 states the boundary relation for the canonical Milnor K-theory elements attached to the degeneracy cycles of generic sections of affine flag bundles.

nodes.title: The nonzero Chern regulator class
nodes.statement: Applying current-regulator-four to the extended cocycle gives a nonzero rational multiple of the suspended universal fourth Chern character in real Deligne/continuous group cohomology. The last logarithmic current constructed from the Milnor-column residues is the transgression of the ordinary fourth Chern class, so is nonzero by G93 Theorem 4.6. Use the supplier’s ch₄=(2πi)^4 pr₄/4! before suspension and ch₄=−c₄/6 on positive K-degrees to fix the rational normalization. Only a nonzero rational multiple is needed; do not infer an integral generator from a rational nonvanishing theorem.
hypotheses: All groups and complexes in this roadmap have rational coefficients; U(F)=F×⊗Z Q.
Combinatorial constructions use an infinite field F. Motivic realizations and the final comparison use a number field F.
proofSteps: Identify the last current as the Chern transgression using the universal vector-bundle flag construction.
Apply G93’s nonvanishing theorem to exclude the zero comparison scalar.
Compare the rest of the cocycle by the residue/current chain identities.
Use request DELIGNE to identify this class with the normalized universal higher regulator, keeping the suspension and rational Chern-character factor.
acceptance: A chain map without this nonvanishing comparison does not suffice to prove the Zagier determinant theorem.

sources.locator: §9.2, Theorem 9.1, p. 87, and item 1, p. 88; §9.3, items 3–5, p. 94
sources.match: Theorem 9.1 asserts that the cocycle represents the universal motivic Chern class and that its Deligne realization gives Beilinson's weight-four regulator; §9.2(1) explains that the successive Milnor-column residues end in a cocycle representing the generator of H⁷(GL_n(C),Z(4)).
Theorem 4.6 shows that the current Σ_j dlog f_j represents a nonzero class in W₀H^{2n−1}(GL_m(C),Q(n)), the transgression of the Chern class.

nodes.title: From K-theory to the explicit complex
nodes.statement: For every number field F and i=1,2,3,4, construct natural maps K_{8−i}(F)⊗Q→H^iΓ-exp(F,4) from the stabilized corrected flag cocycle and rational primitive Hurewicz. For i=1 this is κ:K₇(F)Q→ker δ₄-exp, since the field complex starts in degree one. The maps vanish on the rank-at-most-three homological filtration, proved by the GL₃-invariant standard (N−3)-flag section. This does not assert that a rank filtration equals an Adams filtration, that κ is an isomorphism, or that all higher-K groups in the other degrees are generated by correlators.
hypotheses: All groups and complexes in this roadmap have rational coefficients; U(F)=F×⊗Z Q.
Combinatorial constructions use an infinite field F. Motivic realizations and the final comparison use a number field F.
proofSteps: Pass the natural cohomological flag cocycle through projective-resolution comparison and stabilize.
Restrict stable group homology to rational primitive Hurewicz images from the plus construction (request HOM).
Use the fixed complementary flag section to make the restriction to GL₃ homotopic to a map through the augmentation, hence zero in the positive homological degrees concerned.
For i=1 identify H¹ with the kernel by the supplier’s degree convention.
acceptance: For the weight-four zeta theorem only the i=1 map and its period comparison are required.

nodes.statement: For a number field F and a selection of one embedding σ_j from each complex pair, the vector (Σ_z q_z L₄(σ_jz))_j associated to κ(k)=Σ_z q_z[z]₄ is λπ³ r_Bo,4(k), with λ∈Q× independent of k and F under the fixed universal normalizations. Here r_Bo uses the real-valued Burgos coordinate of the parent; its R(3) Tate coordinate, the normalized Deligne character and the factor-two Borel/Beilinson comparison must all be converted explicitly. In particular this vector has real rank r₂. This statement discharges piece (i) of the parent’s weight-four-regulator-input; it does not by itself prove piece (ii).

nodes.title: The periods of every explicit cycle
nodes.statement: Every y∈ker δ₄-exp(F) has its selected-embedding L₄-period vector in the Q-linear image π³ r_Bo,4(K₇(F)Q). Indeed correlator-realization sends y into the primitive weight-four part of the mixed Tate Lie coalgebra; the canonical primitive identification is Ext¹_MT(F)(Q(0),Q(4))≃K₇(F)Q. Hodge realization, the same period conversion and the regulator comparison give the asserted containment. The vector is allowed to be zero. This supplies piece (ii) of weight-four-regulator-input without asserting κ is surjective or that B₄-comb is inductive B₄.

Invoke MT-1 to identify this primitive with a rational K₇ class; no surjectivity of the combinatorial realization is needed.
Apply the canonical Hodge period and its K-theory compatibility, then cycle-period-calibration and SCALE.
Since multiplication by any nonzero rational leaves a Q-linear image unchanged, the scalar choices do not weaken containment.

nodes.title: The explicit weight-four Zagier theorem
nodes.statement: Let F have r₁ real embeddings, r₂ complex pairs, degree N=r₁+2r₂ and absolute discriminant |D_F|. For every r₂-tuple y₁,…,y_{r₂} of explicit δ₄-cycles, put M_{ij}=L₄(σ_i(y_j)). Then Z₄(y)=π^{4(r₁+r₂)}|D_F|^(−1/2) det M, the parent's zagier-determinant, belongs to Q·ζ_F(4), possibly zero. Some tuple has nonzero determinant and hence Z₄(y)∈Q×ζ_F(4). If r₂>0, rational rescaling of one column gives a tuple with Z₄(y)=ζ_F(4). If r₂=0 the empty determinant is 1 and the assertion is the nonzero rational-ratio identity π^{4r₁}/√|D_F|∈Q×ζ_F(4); no empty column can be rescaled. The parent's totally-real node supplies this case. This discharges the parent's weight-four interface for explicit cycles rather than introducing a second determinant definition.
hypotheses: All groups and complexes in this roadmap have rational coefficients; U(F)=F×⊗Z Q.
Combinatorial constructions use an infinite field F. Motivic realizations and the final comparison use a number field F.
proofSteps: Use κ and Borel's real-regulator isomorphism to choose r₂ rational K₇ vectors whose period determinant is nonzero.
For arbitrary explicit cycles use all-cycle-regulator-image to express their period vectors by a rational matrix in that regulator space.

With d=r₂, Borel's covolume theorem and the leading-term functional equation give det r_Bo∈Q×√|D_F| π^{d−4N}ζ_F(4) on a rational basis; each column contributes π³, giving total exponent 4d−4N=−4(r₁+r₂).

Combine by det_mul for the rational change of basis, using the empty determinant convention separately at r₂=0. The parent's period-calibration is not used: it assumes the period map is an isomorphism onto K₇, which κ need not be.
acceptance: For F=Q the ratio π⁴/ζ_Q(4)=90, so an exact equality with the unrescaled empty determinant would be false.

Vanishing of ω, or a separately proved direct inductive period-containment theorem, is required for the every-inductive-family assertion. Neither is proved here. The weights n≥5 general comparison and Zagier statements are the parent’s conjectural frontier, not consequences of the weight-four extension theorem.

restructure.proposal: Treat ZagierConjecturePolylogarithms as Polylogarithms, Part II, with the six Z-layers owning the proof-specific motivic-correlator, cluster, flag, residue and regulator construction. Dependence runs one way: Z-nodes cite P.3–P.5 objects (explicit B₃, Γ-exp, Z₄, the obstruction ω).
